name: BE Solid Oxide Fuel Cell Valuation
rationale: Bloom Energy Corporation (BE) is the premier manufacturer of solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) with 65% electrical efficiency and a $20B contracted backlog (Oracle, Brookfield, AEP). TTM revenue reached $2.02B with gross margins expanding to 29.0%. At $198.93, our 5-year DCF yields a fair value of $191.34 (-3.8% variance at 10.61% WACC), matching market equilibrium. Reverse DCF indicates the market is pricing in a 60.7% CAGR, reflecting massive datacenter power grid interconnect bypass demand. Recommendation: MAINTAIN (Core Holding: 7.5 shares, 4.61% target weight). Maintain current position size, accumulate only on technical pullbacks near Keltner lower support ($185.31), and take partial profits at Tier 1 resistance ($241.80).

bear.rationale: High manufacturing ramp costs and natural gas supply bottlenecks constrain margins to 10% on $6.18B Y5 revenue.
risks: Natural gas interconnection and pipeline capacity constraints
Competition from modular nuclear reactors and large-scale battery storage

base.rationale: $20B contracted backlog (Oracle, Brookfield, AEP) executes cleanly; 65% electrical efficiency commands premium pricing on $14.38B Y5 revenue.
risks: Manufacturing supply chain bottlenecks in high-density solid oxide materials
Customer concentration across early enterprise AI datacenter commitments

bull.rationale: Bloom SOFC servers become universal baseload standard for gigawatt-scale AI campuses and green hydrogen generation; $27.1B revenue at 22% net margin.
risks: Regulatory review of behind-the-meter emissions standards in California and Texas
Geopolitical trade restrictions on rare-earth inputs for solid oxide electrolytes
